name: The Opened Centre Where Breath Neither Leaves nor Enters
previous_label: Uttanasana — Standing Forward Fold (asana framing, retired 2026-10)

dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24, sequential, one verse per dhāraṇā for 1–16)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: na vrajen na viśec chaktir marudrūpā vikāsite | nirvikalpatayā madhye tayā bhairavarūpatā ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, checked against Singh, Wallis's concordance and Pradīpaka
dharana.rendering: When the centre (madhya) opens out, the power that has the form of breath neither goes out nor comes in; as thought-constructs fall away in that middle, the state of Bhairava appears through her.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer; not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh and Wallis read this as a description of what happens spontaneously when the middle opens. Bäumer (as printed in The Mystery Within) translates it as an instruction ('The Energy of Breath should neither move out nor enter'); Wallis's concordance shows Dyczkowski reading it the same way. This school follows the spontaneous reading and never induces a stop of the breath.
dharana.technique_name: The Opened Centre Where Breath Neither Leaves nor Enters

checked_against: Lakshmanjoo lineage: repose.ghost.io labels verse 26 as meditation 3; not checked in a print Lakshmanjoo edition.
GRETIL, Pradīpaka and Wallis: verse text matches the technique
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dharana number, verified directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against at least one independent edition. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: Y1 (cont.) (Wallis groups verses 24–27 as one technique)

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 26 does not prescribe a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the middle (madhya): the still centre between out-breath and in-breath
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The verse points to one centre, the middle state where breath is neither going out nor coming in and thought thins. It is a point in experience more than a place in the body.
geometry.svg_hint: a single soft point with two faded arrows (out and in) that do not reach it
geometry.honesty: Redefined in 2026-10: geometry now records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Still-centre settle
reaction.summary: School metaphor: busy charge softens into a quiet middle where breath and thought both thin. Not a biochemical claim.

breath.lands_in: the quiet join between out-breath and in-breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Optional: a slightly longer out-breath (about four in, six out) while settling, then stop counting. No forced breath-hold. If the breath pauses on its own, witness it; do not strain into a hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Orient toward the middle, the place between going out and coming in
orientation.gravity: Let weight sink fully into the support; no posture to maintain
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The still point at the middle of the breath (madhya), where inhale and exhale meet and quiet

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: When the centre (madhya) opens out, the power that has the form of breath neither goes out nor comes in; as thought-constructs fall away in that middle, the state of Bhairava appears through her.
adiyogi.method_summary: Rest awareness in the natural still centre where breath-energy is not rushing out or in. Recognise the pause rather than creating it. If breath pauses lightly on its own, witness it; never induce or prolong a stop of the breath.

honesty.disclosure: Door 003 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 3 (verse 26) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type stays school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's. The original honesty text is kept below in honesty.legacy, with retired posture names redacted; the verbatim text is at previous_file.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 003 is dharana 3, verse 26. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
Reframed from the earlier posture framing on 2026-10-06; awaiting guardian re-review. The previous review covered the posture framing only.

legacy.disclosure: This [retired posture]↔method link is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device, not ancient canon. [retired posture] and VBT dharana 003 are paired here by school index.
legacy.notes: Serial pairing by door number. Optional teaching rhyme only: the [retired posture] often quiets outer motion and makes the breath’s middle easier to notice; that rhyme does not upgrade this to inner_logic or claim historical pairing.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Never induce or prolong a stop of the breath for this door. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

legacy_notes.open_seat_alternate: Bend knees generously, hands on blocks or shins, or take [retired posture] ([retired posture] with long spine) if the full hang strains the low back or hamstrings.
legacy_notes.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Soften or exit if sharp low-back, hamstring, or head pressure appears. Avoid forcing straight legs. Use props. If dizziness arises when inverted, come up slowly with a long spine or bent knees.
legacy_notes.status: Posture-specific cautions, kept for traceability; they no longer apply because this door teaches no posture.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 003: the opened centre where breath neither leaves nor enters. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 3, verse 26.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit or lie in any easy way. The map is one point: the middle, between going out and coming in.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the floor take your weight. Eyes closed or lowered. Turn toward the middle.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath. If it helps you settle, four in and six out, then stop counting. No forced breath-hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Rest in the quiet join where the out-breath ends and the in-breath has not begun. Let thoughts thin by themselves.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: busy movement settles into a quiet middle. Metaphor only.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 26: when the centre opens, the breath-power neither goes out nor comes in, and thought-constructs fall away. Witness any natural pause. Never strain.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Take one fuller, free breath. Wriggle the fingers. Open the eyes.
